canal-h2.title: 大运河
trans: China is large, and the north and south are far apart.
The north is cold and the south is hot.
A great deal of rice can be grown in the southern fields.
But getting that rice to the north was very inconvenient.
It took many days on foot, and the road was not safe.
The Sui emperor thought of a great plan.
He decided to make a very long waterway.
This waterway ran all the way from the south to the north.
Many people came to do the work, and it took many years.
The work was hard and tiring, and some never went home again.
But once it was finished, north and south were much closer.
Merchants could go by boat and send goods far away.
Because a boat is faster than walking, goods became cheaper too.
Cities slowly grew up along both banks.
Fourteen hundred years have passed, and people still use it today.

canal2-h2.title: 坐船游玩
trans: Last month my father took me out on a boat.
We got up at six in the morning.
Because it was a long ride, we set out early.
At the river I saw many boats.
Ours was not large, but it was very clean.
When it started moving I felt a little uneasy.
But after a while I felt fine.
The boat moved slowly on the water; it was comfortable.
A breeze came across and it was not hot at all.
I saw many fish in the water.
A few birds in the sky followed us the whole way.
At noon Mother took out the food she had made.
We ate and looked at the hills on either side.
At three in the afternoon the boat returned to the bank.
The day went by fast, and I remember it still.

dongzhou2-h2.title: 猫和老鼠

sents.mn: the back; the rear; the last bit
outside (also pr. [wài mian] for this sense)

trans: Once there were a cat and a mouse, living in one house.
The house was large, with many things in it.
The cat wanted to eat the mouse every day.
But the mouse ran extremely fast.
One morning the cat waited behind the door.
When the mouse came out, the cat sprang.
The moment the mouse saw it, it ran outside.
It ran across the fields, across the river, all the way up the mountain.
Because the mountain path was so long, the cat could run no further.
The cat sat at the foot of the mountain, looking up, saying nothing.
The mouse reached the top and found it was a fine place.
There was water, flowers, and much good food.
And there was no cat there.
So the mouse decided to live there and not go down.
The cat waited a long time, and in the end went home alone.

han-h2.title: 丝绸之路

sents.mn: to know; to become aware of
to like; to be fond of

trans: In the Han dynasty, China had little contact with the lands to the west.
Many people did not know what lay to the west.
Later the emperor sent men west to see what was there.
They travelled for many years before returning.
On their return they said there were many countries to the west, and many new things.
Because of this, Chinese merchants began to travel west too.
They carried Chinese silk, because people in the west liked it very much.
Silk is light and beautiful, and not heavy, so it can be carried far.
The road crossed mountains and very hot places, and was hard going.
One round trip often took a year or two.
Merchants from the west brought things too.
They brought horses, and new fruits.
Not only goods but ideas travelled back and forth along this road.
Because silk was the most famous thing on it, the road came to be called the Silk Road.
This road joined China to places very far away.

han2-h2.title: 我的小猫

sents.mn: to like; to be fond of
although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)
to know; to become aware of

trans: We have a little cat at home called Little White.
It came to us last year, when it was still very small.
It is white all over, with only its eyes black.
Every morning it wakes me up.
If I do not get up, it sits above my head and watches me.
After I get up, the first thing I do is feed it.
It likes fish best, and does not eat much else.
After eating it plays with a ball for a bit.
Sometimes it jumps onto my books and goes to sleep.
Because it is on them, I cannot read.
When I leave for school it watches me from the door.
When I come home in the afternoon it runs over and gives a cry.
Although it cannot speak, I know it is glad.
At night it sleeps by my bed, without stirring.
I love my little cat; it is my best friend.

konfucius-h2.title: 孔子的学生

sents.mn: to know; to become aware of
although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)
to know; to become aware of

trans: More than two thousand five hundred years ago, there was a teacher in China.
His name was Confucius.
In those days, only the wealthy could study.
But Confucius said he would teach anyone who wanted to learn.
So his students grew more and more numerous.
Among his students were grown men and very young people.
They read together, talked together and walked together.
Confucius often said: "After you learn, think it over often."
He also said: "If you do not know a thing, simply ask."
A student asked him: "What is a good person?"
He said: "Do not give others what you would not want yourself."
Although he long wanted to serve as an official, he did not succeed.
So he put all his time into teaching.
After he died, his students wrote down what he had said.
Because of that book, we still know his thinking today.

paper-h2.title: 纸的故事
trans: Long ago people did not write on paper, because there was none.
They wrote on strips of bamboo.
One book took a great deal of bamboo.
So a book was heavy and bulky, and one person could not carry it.
If you wanted to send a friend a book, it was a hard thing to do.
Later a man thought of a way.
His name was Cai Lun.
He took tree bark and old cloth and put them in water.
Then he worked them until they were white and light.
Once dry, it became paper.
Paper is light, and not expensive.
With paper, students could carry books to school.
Teachers could write out lessons for everyone to read.
Because paper was so useful, it slowly reached other countries.
Today people all over the world use paper, and it began in China.

paper2-h2.title: 书里的世界

sents.mn: to like; to be fond of
although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)

trans: My favourite thing is books.
My room is full of books, all over the place.
Some are new, some are already old.
Books hold many interesting stories.
Some are about things from long ago.
In them are emperors, the Great Wall, and Dayu.
Some are about the animals of the sky and the water.
When I read, it is as if I have gone somewhere far away.
Sometimes I read so intently that I do not hear my mother call.
She says: "Reading makes you a better person."
She also says I can ask her about any character I do not know.
So I often keep a small notebook to hand.
When I meet a new character, I write it down.
Every evening I read for a while.
Although I have already read many books, I want to read more.

qin-h2.title: 万里长城

sents.mn: although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)

trans: More than two thousand years ago, China had many small states.
These states fought one another constantly, and life was hard for everyone.
Later one man brought them all together.
He was Qin Shi Huang, China’s first emperor.
He did a great many things.
He made every place use the same characters.
He made everyone use the same money.
Because people often came across from the north, he was uneasy.
He decided to build a very long wall in the north.
Many people came to do this work, and it went on for many years.
They laid the earth and timber up piece by piece.
Although the work was tiring and hard, they did not stop.
The wall runs along the mountains, with no end in sight.
Because it is so long, it is called the Ten-Thousand-Li Great Wall.
More than two thousand years have passed, and we can still go and see it.

qin2-h2.title: 爬山的孩子

sents.mn: to think that ...; to feel that ...
although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)

trans: Last month the teacher took us climbing.
The morning weather was fine, and not hot at all.
We met at the school gate at eight.
Twenty of us went in all.
The mountain path was long, with trees on both sides.
We walked and talked at the same time.
After an hour I began to feel tired.
I sat under a tree and drank some water.
I said: "I don’t want to walk any more."
A friend came over and said: "We are nearly there."
He said: "If we go back now, we won’t see what is up there."
I thought about it, then stood up.
We walked another half hour, and at last reached the top.
Looking down from up there, the school was as small as a dot.
Although I was tired, I was glad I had not turned back.

sanguo-h2.title: 诸葛亮的智慧

sents.mn: Liu Bei, a ruler he served
to know; to become aware of
to think that ...; to feel that ...
to think (i.e. to take it to be true that ...) (Usually there is an implication that the notion is mistaken – except when expressing one's own current opinion.)

trans: After the Han, China split into three states.
The three states fought one another constantly.
There was a very clever man of that time called Zhuge Liang.
When he was young he lived in the hills and read every day.
Liu Bei went to ask him three times before he came out to serve.
Because he knew so much, everyone listened to him.
He could read the weather, and could find a way.
Once the enemy came, but there were few soldiers in the city.
Everyone was uneasy.
Zhuge Liang did not close the gates, and sat alone up on the wall.
When the enemy arrived and saw the gates open, they thought it strange.
They supposed the city must be full of soldiers.
So they did not go in, and left.
He served his state until he was very old.
To this day many people still tell his story.

sanguo2-h2.title: 好朋友的力量

sents.mn: to think that ...; to feel that ...
to think that ...; to feel that ...

trans: I have three very good friends.
We are at the same school and in the same class.
Every day at noon the four of us eat together.
After class we often play together too.
Sometimes we do not think the same way.
But after talking it over, it is soon fine again.
Last month I fell ill and could not go to school.
I was at home alone, and it felt very dull.
On the third day the three of them came to see me.
They brought fruit, and two books.
They sat by my bed and talked about what was happening at school.
Hearing it made me happy, and I forgot at once that I was ill.
As they left they said: "Get well soon."
By the next morning I already felt much better.
I think good friends really can make a person well.

shang-h2.title: 骨头上的字

sents.mn: to be convinced (that sth is true); to believe; to accept sth as true
to know; to become aware of

trans: The Shang was one of China’s very early dynasties.
People of that time could already write.
But they did not write on paper, because there was no paper yet.
They wrote the characters on animal bones.
These bones were large and white, and many characters could be written on them.
Shang people believed there were gods in the sky.
So when they had a question, they asked the gods.
They asked: "Will the weather be good today?"
They also asked: "Will this journey go well?"
After asking, they burned the bone with fire.
Lines would appear on the bone, and they read the lines for the answer.
Then they wrote both the question and the answer on that bone.
These are China’s earliest characters, more than three thousand years old.
Long afterwards, people found these bones in the ground.
So today we can still see the characters the Shang people wrote.

shang2-h2.title: 市场的一天

sents.mn: to think that ...; to feel that ...
although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)

trans: Today is market day.
Mother woke me up very early.
She said: "If we go late, the good things will be gone."
We left at eight, and it took twenty minutes to get there.
There were already many people at the market.
Some sold fruit, some sold fish, and some sold vegetables.
The fruit seller said: "Today’s apples are red and delicious."
I looked, and thought he was right.
Mother asked how much they cost, then bought six.
We went to the fish stall as well.
The fish there was fresh, because it had only arrived that morning.
There were more and more things, so I carried two bags for her.
On the way home we bought two pieces of bread.
Once home, Mother started to cook.
Although we walked a lot today, I was very happy.

shufa-h2.title: 写字高手

sents.mn: to think that ...; to feel that ...

trans: Chinese people early on felt that writing was a beautiful thing.
More than sixteen hundred years ago there was a very famous man.
His name was Wang Xizhi.
He began learning to write when he was very young.
He practised every day, and never stopped for a single day.
After writing he would go to the water’s edge to wash his brush.
Because he did this for so many years, the water there turned black.
The characters he wrote were extremely beautiful.
Some were like wind, some like water.
So people called him the Sage of Calligraphy.
One year he met many friends in the mountains.
The weather that day was fine, and they drank and wrote poems.
He gathered everyone’s poems together and wrote a few lines of his own.
Those few lines became the most famous writing in China.
To this day many people still study his way of writing.

shufa2-h2.title: 学写汉字

sents.mn: to think that ...; to feel that ...

trans: This month we began learning to write Chinese characters.
The teacher first taught us how to hold the pen.
She said: "Sit up straight, and your characters will look better."
She also said not to write too fast.
We started with the two characters for water and mountain.
These two look easy, but writing them well is not.
Because a character has many strokes, which one comes first matters.
I wrote one character more than thirty times.
At first I wrote them badly.
But day by day I wrote them better and better.
The teacher looked and said: "Much better than last month."
I showed the best one to my mother.
She said it was lovely, and put it up in her room.
Now I want to write a little every day.
I feel every character is interesting.

tao-h2.title: 田里的诗人

sents.mn: to like; to be fond of
to think that ...; to feel that ...
although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)
to think that ...; to feel that ...

trans: More than sixteen hundred years ago there was a famous poet.
When he was young he had served as an official.
An official could have money, and could have a name.
But he did not like that kind of life at all.
He felt he had to say things every day that he did not want to say.
So one day he decided to stop.
He went back to his own home and began to farm.
He grew rice and vegetables, and many flowers as well.
In the morning he worked in the fields; in the evening he wrote poems.
His poems were not long, but beautiful.
In them he said that in the fields his heart was free.
Although his family was not rich, he lived happily.
Someone asked him: "Did you feel it had been the right thing?"
He said: "I do not want much; this is enough."
More than a thousand years have passed, and Chinese people still read his poems.

tao2-h2.title: 下雨天

sents.mn: outside (also pr. [wài mian] for this sense)
to think that ...; to feel that ...
outside (also pr. [wài mian] for this sense)

trans: This morning, the moment I got up I saw the sky was dark.
A little later it began to rain.
The rain grew heavier, so I could not go out to play.
I sat by the window and looked outside.
The rain struck the ground with a lovely sound.
People in the street were all walking fast.
A child ran past, soaked through.
At first I felt a little bored.
Then I decided to read at home.
Mother made me something hot to drink.
She took a book too, and sat down in front of me.
Neither of us spoke, and the room was pleasant.
By the afternoon the rain slowly eased.
The sky brightened a little, and outside looked clean.
I think a rainy day has its good side too.

xia-h2.title: 大禹治水

sents.mn: bar (loanword) (serving drinks, or providing Internet access etc)
although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)

trans: Very long ago, it rained in China for many days.
Because there was so much rain, the water rose higher and higher.
The water came into the fields, and into many people’s homes.
People had nowhere to live, and could only move up the mountains.
The king of that time was uneasy, and asked everyone what should be done.
Someone said: "Dayu is a good man — let him come."
After Dayu came, he first went to look at the water, and only then began work.
He found that if you only shut the water in with earth, it would come back.
So he decided to open a road for the water, letting it flow out to the sea.
He did this together with many others, and it went on for thirteen years.
Although he missed home, he never went back.
Three times he came to his own door, and did not go in.
Later the water went down, and everyone returned to plant in the fields.
Because he had done this, the king gave his place to him.
To this day, Chinese people still tell the story of Dayu.

xia2-h2.title: 小龙学游泳

sents.mn: particle indicating that a previously asked question is to be applied to the preceding word ("What about ...?", "And ...?")
although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)

trans: There was a river in the mountains, and many dragons lived in it.
Among them was a little dragon who could not yet swim.
Every morning it sat by the river and watched the other dragons.
The others leapt and played in the water, and looked very happy.
Little Dragon wanted to go in too, but did not dare.
Because the water was deep and cold, it kept sitting there.
Its mother asked: "Why don’t you come in?"
Little Dragon said: "I don’t dare. If I go in, will something bad happen?"
Its mother said: "Watch me first — I will teach you."
Then its mother swam slowly in the water for it to see.
Little Dragon watched for a long time, and at last went into the water too.
The first time it did not do well, and its head went under the water.
Even so, it tried again, and again.
By the afternoon it could already swim to the other side of the river.
Its mother said: "You see — you did it yourself."

zhou-h2.title: 天命的故事

sents.mn: although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)

trans: After the Shang, China had a new dynasty called the Western Zhou.
The Western Zhou king wanted everyone to listen to him.
So he said something that became very famous.
He said: "It is Heaven that made me king."
He also said that Heaven is always watching every king.
If a king does well, Heaven lets him go on.
If a king does badly, Heaven gives the place to someone else.
So a king cannot think only of himself.
He must care about the farmers, and about the soldiers.
In those days many people worked in the fields.
Because the weather was good, a great deal was grown.
There was rice and meat at home, and life was not bad.
The king made many new rules, and everyone had to follow them.
Although the Western Zhou later ended, this idea remained.
To this day Chinese people still speak of the "Mandate of Heaven".

zhou2-h2.title: 大树下的朋友

sents.mn: although; even though (often used correlatively with 是 or 是 etc)
to like; to be fond of
to like; to be fond of

trans: There is a very big tree at our school gate.
The tree is already old — older than the school.
It is tall, and it is pleasant underneath when the weather is hot.
So every day at noon we play under it.
My three friends and I often go over together.
Sometimes we play games, and sometimes we tell stories.
One of them is very good at telling stories.
When he tells one, everybody goes quiet.
Today he told a very long story.
In the story there were mountains, water, and a dragon.
We listened closely, because the story was so good.
Then the teacher came over and said: "It is time for class."
We ran back to the classroom, sat down and took out our books.
Although the story was not finished, we can hear the rest tomorrow.
I love that tree, and I love those friends.
